_comment: Guiones de clase de en-es. 'target' es lo que el profe dice en español -el idioma que se aprende, el que pronuncia la voz meta- y 'native' el andamiaje en ingles. La fonetica esta escrita para un lector de ingles: silaba tonica en mayusculas. Generado por tools/, ver el encabezado del script.

moves.native: Hello! Welcome to your first class.

moves.target: Hoy vamos a saludar y a decir tu nombre.
moves.native: Today we're going to say hello and give your name.

moves.target: Escuchá primero. No importa si no entendés todo.
moves.native: Listen first. Don't worry if you don't catch everything.
Hello. The H is silent — always, in every Spanish word.
Good morning. Used until about two in the afternoon.
Good afternoon — which starts after lunch, not at noon.
My name is. The double L sounds like the Y in yes.

moves.target: Escuchá la frase entera: «Hola, me llamo Capy».
moves.native: Listen to the whole thing: Hola, me llamo Capy.

moves.target: Hoy aprendiste a saludar y a decir tu nombre.
moves.native: Today you learned to greet someone and give your name.

practice.native: Greet me.
Tell me your name: me llamo and then your name.

practice.target: Saludame como si fuera de mañana.
practice.native: Greet me as if it were morning.
And now, in the afternoon.
Introduce yourself to me.

moves.target: Te voy a ayudar un poco menos en inglés.
moves.native: I'll help you a bit less in English today.
How are you? Not a real question — the answer is bien.
And you? In Argentina vos replaces tú.

moves.target: Ya podés saludar, decir tu nombre y preguntar cómo está alguien.
moves.native: You can now greet someone, give your name and ask how they are.

practice.native: Ask me how I am.
I'm asking you: ¿cómo estás?
Tell me your name again.
Greet me and introduce yourself, all in one go.

moves.target: Hoy juntamos todo lo de esta semana.
moves.native: Today we put the whole week together.
Nice to meet you. Literally: much pleasure.
All together now — don't worry about being perfect.

moves.target: Con esto ya podés empezar una conversación con cualquiera.
moves.native: With this you can already open a conversation with anyone.

practice.native: We've just met. What do you say?
Greet me.

practice.target: Conocés a alguien nuevo. Decile todo.
practice.native: You're meeting someone new. Say the whole thing.

moves.target: Las cinco vocales del español no cambian nunca.
moves.native: Spanish has five vowel sounds and they never change. That's why you can read anything.

moves.target: Del uno al cinco. Mañana llegamos al diez.
moves.native: One to five. Tomorrow we get to ten.

practice.native: How many hands do you have?
How many fingers on one hand?
Count to three.
Count from one to five.

moves.native: Let's carry on with the numbers.

practice.native: How many fingers altogether?
How many days in a week?

practice.target: Un número entre siete y nueve.
practice.native: A number between seven and nine.
Count from one to ten.

moves.target: Última clase de la unidad. Juntamos saludos y números.
moves.native: Last class of the unit. We put greetings and numbers together.
My phone number is. Now the numbers do real work.

moves.target: Ya podés presentarte y dar tu teléfono. Eso es una conversación real.
moves.native: You can now introduce yourself and give your phone number. That's a real conversation.

practice.native: Give me your phone number.
And your name.
Introduce yourself and give me your number.

moves.target: Unidad dos. Hoy hablamos de tu familia.
moves.native: Unit two. Today we talk about your family.
My brother. The H is silent again.
My sister. Only the last vowel changes.
My parents — not my fathers. The masculine plural covers both.

moves.target: Fijate: mis, con ese, porque los padres son dos.
moves.native: Notice mis with an S: the possessive agrees with what you own, not with you.

moves.target: Ya podés nombrar a tu familia.
moves.native: You can now name your family.

practice.native: Tell me about your mother.
Do you have a sister?
Name them both together.

practice.target: Contame quién vive en tu casa.
practice.native: Tell me who lives in your house.

moves.target: Hoy practicamos la familia y sumamos tener.
moves.native: Today we practise family and add the verb tener.
I don't have. The no simply goes in front — there's no do or don't in Spanish.

moves.target: Tengo, no tengo, ¿tenés? Con eso ya preguntás y respondés.
moves.native: Tengo, no tengo, ¿tenés? That's enough to ask and answer.

practice.native: Tell me how many siblings you have.
Do you have sisters? If not, say so.
Ask me.
Describe your family using tengo.

moves.target: Cerramos la semana juntando familia y números.
moves.native: We close the week joining family and numbers.
Years old. The ñ is the ni in onion.

moves.target: En español la edad se tiene, no se es: tengo treinta años.
moves.native: In Spanish you HAVE years, you aren't them: tengo treinta años.

practice.native: Tell me your age — remember: tengo.
How many siblings?

practice.target: Presentá a tu familia con edades.
practice.native: Introduce your family with their ages.

moves.native: I live in. The V sounds like a soft B.

moves.target: Soy de, vivo en, hablo. Tres verbos que vas a usar todos los días.
moves.native: Soy de, vivo en, hablo. Three verbs you'll use every day.

practice.native: Where are you from?
And where do you live now?
What languages do you speak?

practice.target: Contame de dónde sos y dónde vivís.
practice.native: Tell me where you're from and where you live.

moves.target: Practicamos el origen y sumamos el trabajo.
moves.native: We practise origin and add work.
I work at. The J is a throaty H.
I am — for professions, with no article. Soy médico, not soy un médico.

moves.target: Sin artículo: soy profesor, no soy un profesor.
moves.native: No article: soy profesor, never soy un profesor.

practice.native: What do you do for a living?
Where do you work?
Are you studying anything?

practice.target: Decime tu trabajo, sin el artículo.
practice.native: Tell me your job — remember, no article.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Presentación completa.
moves.native: Last one of the unit. Full introduction.
Delighted — a man says encantado, a woman encantada.

moves.target: Nombre, origen, trabajo y edad. Eso es presentarse de verdad.
moves.native: Name, origin, job and age. That's a real introduction.

practice.native: I'm introducing you to someone. What do you say?
Your whole background.

practice.target: Presentate entero: nombre, origen, trabajo, edad.
practice.native: Full introduction: name, origin, job, age.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Unidad tres. Hoy: dónde están las cosas.
moves.native: Unit three. Today: where things are.
Is — for location and for how something is right now.
In, on and at, all in one word. Spanish doesn't make you choose.

moves.target: Para lugares siempre está, nunca es. Madrid está en España.
moves.native: Location always takes está, never es — even for something as permanent as a city.

moves.target: Está, en, aquí, allí. Con eso ubicás cualquier cosa.
moves.native: Está, en, aquí, allí. That's enough to locate anything.

practice.native: Where is your phone?
It's in your hand. Say so.
Ask me where the bathroom is.
Tell me where you are right now.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Hoy sumamos hay, que sirve para todo.
moves.native: Today we add hay, which does a lot of work.
There is AND there are. One word, never plural.

moves.target: Hay para lo que existe. Está para lo que ya conocés.
moves.native: Hay introduces something new; está locates something already known.

moves.target: Hay un banco. El banco está en la esquina. Distinto.
moves.native: Hay un banco versus el banco está en la esquina. Different jobs.

practice.native: What is there in your neighbourhood?
Is there a pool? If not, say so.
Do you live near the centre?

practice.target: Contame qué hay cerca de tu casa.
practice.native: Tell me what there is near your house.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Cerramos la semana con la hora.
moves.native: We close the week with telling the time.
It's — plural, because you're counting hours.
It's one o'clock — the only singular hour.

moves.target: Son las tres, pero es la una. El uno es la excepción.
moves.native: Son las tres, but es la una. One is the exception.

practice.native: Ask me the time.
It's five o'clock. Say it.
And now one o'clock.

practice.target: Decime a qué hora te levantás.
practice.native: Tell me what time you get up.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Segunda semana. Tu día, de la mañana a la noche.
moves.native: Second week. Your day, morning to night.
I get up. The me isn't optional — without it you're lifting something else.

moves.target: Fijate en el me. Levanto es levantar algo; me levanto soy yo.
moves.native: Watch the me: levanto means I lift something, me levanto means I get myself up.

moves.target: Cinco verbos y ya podés contar todo tu día.
moves.native: Five verbs and you can already narrate your whole day.

practice.native: What time do you get up?
Where do you work?
And what time do you go to bed?

practice.target: Contame tu día desde que te levantás.
practice.native: Tell me your day from the moment you get up.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Practicamos la rutina y vemos las tres familias de verbos.
moves.native: We practise the routine and look at the three verb families.
Do you work? No do — the verb alone asks.

moves.target: Hablo, como, vivo. Tres terminaciones y ya está el presente.
moves.native: Hablo, como, vivo. Three endings and you have the present tense.

practice.native: What languages do you speak?
Where do you live?
Ask me if I work.

practice.target: Contame dónde vivís y qué hacés.
practice.native: Tell me where you live and what you do.

scripts.focus: Your day and where things are

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Tu día completo, con horas y lugares.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Your full day, with times and places.
At — for scheduling. Son las ocho tells the time; a las ocho schedules it.

moves.target: Son las para decir la hora, a las para agendar. No es lo mismo.
moves.native: Son las tells the time; a las schedules. Not the same thing.

practice.native: What time do you start work?

practice.target: Y a qué hora te levantás.
practice.native: And what time you get up.
Your whole day, with the times.

moves.target: Unidad cuatro. Hoy salimos a la calle.
moves.native: Unit four. Today we go out into the street.

moves.target: Cuidado: derecha es el lado; derecho es seguir de frente.
moves.native: Careful: derecha is the direction right, derecho is straight ahead. One vowel apart.

moves.target: Con esto pedís y entendés una dirección.
moves.native: With this you can ask for and follow directions.

practice.target: Parás a alguien en la calle. ¿Qué decís?
practice.native: You stop someone in the street. What do you say?
Send me to the right.
And now straight ahead.

practice.target: Pedime cómo llegar a la estación.
practice.native: Ask me how to get to the station.

moves.target: Hoy: este, ese y aquel. Tres, no dos.
moves.native: Today: este, ese and aquel. Three, not two.
That — near YOU, the person I'm talking to.
That one over there — far from both of us.
This thing, when you don't know what it is yet.

moves.target: Ese no es distancia: es lo que está cerca del otro.
moves.native: Ese isn't about measured distance — it's anchored to the listener.

moves.target: El inglés tiene dos. El español tiene tres.
moves.native: English splits the world in two. Spanish splits it in three.

practice.target: Señalá algo que tengas en la mano.
practice.native: Point at something in your hand.
Something I'm holding.
You don't know what it is. Ask.
Ask me for something by pointing at it.

moves.target: Cerramos con poder, que sirve para pedir.
moves.native: We close with poder, which is how you ask for things.
May I? Same word — the question does the asking.

moves.target: Poder va seguido del infinitivo, sin nada en el medio.
moves.native: Poder is followed straight by an infinitive, nothing in between.

practice.native: Ask permission to come in.
Ask me for help.
Tell me something you can do.
Ask me a favour using podés.

moves.native: How much are they? The verb agrees.
Do you have? — formal, to a shopkeeper.

moves.target: Ojo con los precios escritos: la coma es el decimal.
moves.native: Watch written prices: the comma is the decimal point. 2,50 is two fifty.

moves.target: Preguntar el precio, decir si es caro, pedir lo que buscás.
moves.native: Ask the price, say if it's dear, ask for what you're after.

practice.native: Ask about a coffee.
And now about some shoes.
They say a hundred euros. React.
Buy something from me: ask and decide.

moves.target: Practicamos la compra y sumamos pagar.
moves.native: We practise shopping and add paying.
I want — direct. Add por favor.
I would like — much politer. Use this in shops.

moves.target: Quisiera en vez de quiero. Un cambio chico, otra impresión.
moves.native: Quisiera instead of quiero. Small change, very different impression.

practice.native: Ask for a table for two.
They ask how you're paying.

practice.target: Pedí un café, con por favor.
practice.native: Order a coffee, with please.
Order something in a restaurant.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Salir, preguntar y comprar.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Going out, asking and buying.

moves.target: Ya podés entrar a un negocio y salir con lo que querías.
moves.native: You can now walk into a shop and come out with what you wanted.

practice.native: They hand you what you asked for.
Ask for something else.

practice.target: Toda la escena: entrás, preguntás, comprás, agradecés.
practice.native: The whole scene: come in, ask, buy, thank them.

moves.target: Unidad cinco. Hoy la frase se da vuelta.
moves.native: Unit five. Today the sentence turns around.
I like it — literally, it is pleasing to me.

moves.target: Yo gusto no es «me gusta». Significa que le caigo bien a la gente.
moves.native: Yo gusto doesn't mean I like — it means people find me attractive.

moves.target: El verbo concuerda con la cosa, no con vos.
moves.native: The verb agrees with the thing liked, not with you.

practice.native: Do you like coffee?
And tea?
Ask me.

practice.target: Decime tres cosas que te gustan.
practice.native: Tell me three things you like.

moves.target: Hoy: cuando la cosa es plural.
moves.native: Today: when the thing liked is plural.
I like them — plural thing, plural verb.
I like reading — an infinitive is always singular.

moves.target: Gusta o gustan lo decide la cosa. Vos no entrás en esa cuenta.
moves.native: Gusta or gustan is decided by the thing. You don't come into it.

practice.native: Do you like dogs?
Do you like reading?
Ask me about films.

practice.target: Contame qué cosas te gustan, en plural.
practice.native: Tell me what things you like, in the plural.

moves.target: Cerramos con la familia de gustar.
moves.native: We close with the gustar family.
I love it. Never say me encanta mucho — it already is the most.

moves.target: Todos funcionan igual: la cosa manda, vos sos el que recibe.
moves.native: They all work the same way: the thing is the subject, you're the receiver.

practice.native: Something you love.
Something that annoys you.
A subject that interests you.

practice.target: Contame algo que te encanta y por qué.
practice.native: Tell me something you love and why.

moves.native: Why — two words with an accent. Porque, one word, means because.

moves.target: Todas llevan tilde cuando preguntan. No es adorno.
moves.native: They all take a written accent when asking. It's not decoration.

moves.target: Cinco preguntas y ya sostenés una conversación.
moves.native: Five question words and you can hold a conversation.

practice.native: Ask me where I live.
Ask me when I work.
Ask me why.
Ask me three different questions.

moves.target: Hoy la pregunta que casi todos hacen mal.
moves.native: Today, the question almost everyone gets wrong.
What's your name. Cuál, not qué, before ser.

moves.target: Qué es tu nombre pregunta qué es un nombre. Se dice cuál.
moves.native: ¿Qué es tu nombre? asks what a name IS. You want ¿cuál es tu nombre?

practice.native: Ask me my name, properly.
Ask how many siblings I have.
Ask me how I am.
Interview me: four questions.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Gustos y preguntas juntos.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Likes and questions together.
Because — one word, no accent. Never starts a sentence.

moves.target: Por qué pregunta, porque responde. Se escriben distinto.
moves.native: Por qué asks, porque answers. Different spellings.

practice.target: Te pregunto por qué te gusta. Respondé.
practice.native: I ask why you like it. Answer.

practice.target: Algo que te gusta, con motivo.
practice.native: Something you like, with a reason.

practice.target: Contame un gusto tuyo y explicá por qué.
practice.native: Tell me something you like and explain why.

moves.native: Big — same for masculine and feminine.
Small — this one changes: pequeña for feminine.
The same word for a feminine noun.

moves.target: El adjetivo va después: una casa bonita, no una bonita casa.
moves.native: The adjective goes after the noun: una casa bonita. That's the default.

moves.target: El adjetivo copia el género del sustantivo. En inglés no pasa nada de esto.
moves.native: The adjective copies the noun's gender. English never asks you to do this.

practice.native: Describe your house.
A nice photo. Say it — watch the ending.
Something you bought recently.
Describe the place where you live.

moves.native: Add -es after a consonant. Fácil becomes fáciles.
A final Z turns into C: feliz, felices.

moves.target: Género y número. Todo en la frase se alinea con el sustantivo.
moves.native: Gender and number. Everything in the phrase lines up with the noun.

practice.native: Some nice shoes.
Two easy exercises.
The children are happy.
Describe three things, in the plural.

moves.target: Cerramos con cada cuánto hacés las cosas.
moves.native: We close with how often you do things.

moves.target: No como nunca carne. Dos negativos en español se refuerzan.
moves.native: No como nunca carne. Two negatives reinforce each other in Spanish.

practice.target: Algo que hacés todos los días.
practice.native: Something you do every day.
Something you never do.

practice.target: Y algo de vez en cuando.
practice.native: And something now and then.

practice.target: Contame tus costumbres con estas tres.
practice.native: Describe your habits using these three.

moves.native: More than. There's no -er ending in Spanish.

moves.target: Antes de un número va de, no que: más de veinte.
moves.native: Before a number it's más DE, not más que. Más de veinte personas.

moves.target: Un solo molde para todos los adjetivos. Eso es más fácil que el inglés.
moves.native: One frame for every adjective. That part is easier than English.

practice.native: Compare two cities.
Which one is better?
Two things that are equal.
Compare your city with another one.

moves.native: We practise and get to the superlative.
In, for superlatives: el mejor DE la ciudad, not en la ciudad.

moves.target: El mejor de la clase. Con de, no con en.
moves.native: El mejor de la clase — with de, where English uses in.

practice.native: The best restaurant you know.

practice.target: La cosa más cara que compraste.
practice.native: The most expensive thing you've bought.

practice.target: El más alto de tu familia.
practice.native: The tallest in your family.

practice.target: Contame lo mejor de tu ciudad.
practice.native: Tell me the best thing about your city.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Describir y comparar todo junto.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Describing and comparing together.
Absolutely great. Never muy buenísimo — the ending already means very.

moves.target: Buenísimo suena a alguien que habla, no a alguien que estudia.
moves.native: Buenísimo sounds like someone who speaks the language, not someone studying it.

practice.native: The food was excellent. Say it.
Compare two meals.

practice.target: Contame de un lugar que te encantó.
practice.native: Tell me about a place you loved.

moves.target: Unidad siete. Hoy empezamos a hablar del pasado.
moves.native: Unit seven. Today we start talking about the past.
I spoke. The accent is not decoration: hablo is I speak, habló is he spoke.
I went out. The -er and -ir endings are identical — that halves the work.

moves.target: La tilde cambia el tiempo y la persona. No es un detalle.
moves.native: The accent changes both the tense and the person. It is doing real work.

moves.target: Este pasado es para algo terminado, visto como un bloque.
moves.native: This past is for something finished, seen as one whole block.

practice.native: What did you eat yesterday?
Who did you speak to today?
Did you go out last night?
Tell me what you did yesterday.

moves.target: Hoy los irregulares, que son los que más se usan.
moves.native: Today the irregular ones, which are the ones you'll use most.
I went AND I was. Ser and ir share this whole tense — context decides.

moves.target: Estos no llevan tilde: tuve, no tuvé.
moves.native: These carry no accent at all: tuve, never tuvé. Different endings from the regular ones.

moves.target: Fui de Madrid y fui a Madrid. La misma palabra, dos verbos.
moves.native: Fui médico and fui a Madrid. Same word, two different verbs.

practice.native: Where did you go at the weekend?
Did you have to work?
What did you do on Sunday?
Tell me about your weekend.

moves.target: Cerramos con hace, que va adelante.
moves.native: We close with hace, which goes at the front.
Ago — but it goes FIRST. Hace dos años, not dos años hace.
Since — for a point in time.

moves.target: Para algo que sigue pasando se usa el presente: hace dos años que vivo acá.
moves.native: For something still going on, use the present: hace dos años que vivo aquí.

practice.native: When did you arrive?
How long have you been studying Spanish?
Since when have you lived there?

practice.target: Contame hace cuánto que hacés algo.
practice.native: Tell me how long you've been doing something.

moves.target: Segunda semana: el futuro de todos los días.

moves.native: I'm going to. The a is not optional — voy comer is wrong.

moves.target: Esto se usa mucho más que el futuro de los libros.
moves.native: This is far more common in speech than the future tense the textbooks teach.

moves.target: Ir más a más infinitivo. Con eso hablás del futuro sin aprender otro tiempo.
moves.native: Ir + a + infinitive. That's the future, without learning another tense.

practice.native: What are you going to do tomorrow?
Suggest something for Saturday.
Ask me about my plans.

practice.target: Contame tus planes del fin de semana.
practice.native: Tell me your plans for the weekend.

moves.target: Hoy los pronombres, que van adelante del verbo.
moves.native: Today the pronouns, which go in FRONT of the verb.
It, him — and it goes before the verb. Lo veo, never veo lo.
I don't know. Lo stands for the whole idea.

moves.target: Con infinitivo podés pegarlo atrás: voy a comprarlo o lo voy a comprar.
moves.native: With an infinitive you have a choice: voy a comprarlo or lo voy a comprar. Both correct.

moves.target: El inglés pone el objeto atrás. El español pone el pronombre adelante.
moves.native: English puts the object after. Spanish puts the pronoun in front.

practice.target: Te pregunto por el libro. Ya lo compraste.
practice.native: I ask about the book. You already bought it.
Promise you'll call me.

practice.target: Te pregunto algo que no sabés.
practice.native: I ask you something you don't know.

practice.target: Contestame usando lo o la, sin repetir la cosa.
practice.native: Answer me using lo or la, without repeating the thing.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Ayer, hoy y mañana juntos.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Yesterday, today and tomorrow together.

moves.target: Con primero y después ya contás una historia, no una lista.
moves.native: With primero and después you're telling a story, not reciting a list.

practice.target: Empezá a contarme tu día de ayer.
practice.native: Start telling me about your day yesterday.
And carry on.

practice.target: Contame ayer y mañana, en orden.
practice.native: Tell me about yesterday and tomorrow, in order.

moves.target: Unidad ocho. El otro pasado, el más fácil de todos.
moves.native: Unit eight. The other past — the easiest tense in Spanish.
I used to speak. Every -ar verb takes this -aba shape.
I used to eat. Every -er and -ir verb takes -ía.
Always — a signal for this tense.

moves.target: Solo tres verbos son irregulares en todo el idioma: ser, ir y ver.
moves.native: Only three verbs are irregular here in the whole language: ser, ir and ver. That's the complete list.

moves.target: Este pasado no tiene bordes: es lo que pasaba, no lo que pasó.
moves.native: This past has no edges: it's what used to happen, not what happened.

practice.native: What did you use to do as a child?
Where did you live before?
What did you eat on Sundays?
Tell me what your childhood was like.

moves.target: Hoy los tres irregulares. Son tres y se acabó.
moves.native: Today the three irregulars. Three, and that's the lot.
I was, it was — from ser.
I had — regular, even though tener is wild elsewhere.

moves.target: Tenía diez años. La edad en pasado siempre va acá.
moves.native: Tenía diez años. Age in the past always takes this tense.

practice.native: What was your school like?
How did you use to get to school?
How old were you?

practice.target: Describime un lugar de tu infancia.
practice.native: Describe a place from your childhood.

moves.target: Cerramos con la decisión difícil: cuál de los dos pasados.
moves.native: We close with the hard choice: which of the two pasts.
When — the word that usually joins the two.

moves.target: El imperfecto pinta la escena, el pretérito la rompe: leía cuando sonó el teléfono.
moves.native: The imperfect paints the scene, the preterite breaks it: leía cuando sonó el teléfono.

practice.native: Tell me about something that interrupted you.
Two things at the same time.

practice.target: Contame una anécdota con los dos pasados.
practice.native: Tell me a short story using both past tenses.

moves.native: I have to — the everyday one.
I ought to — heavier, more moral.
One has to — impersonal, obliges nobody in particular.
You should — advice, not an order.

moves.target: Hay que no tiene sujeto. No podés decir yo hay que.
moves.native: Hay que has no subject at all. You can't say yo hay que — use tengo que.

moves.target: Tengo que para vos, hay que para todos, deberías para aconsejar.
moves.native: Tengo que for you, hay que for everyone, deberías to advise.

practice.native: What do you have to do today?

practice.target: Una regla del lugar donde trabajás.
practice.native: A rule where you work.
Give me a piece of advice.

practice.target: Contame tus obligaciones de esta semana.
practice.native: Tell me your obligations this week.

moves.target: Hoy: a quién. Los pronombres que dicen para quién.
moves.native: Today: to whom. The pronouns that say who receives.
To him, to her, to you — one form, no gender.
Le becomes se before lo. Le lo simply doesn't exist.
Can you pass it to me?

moves.target: En español se dice el pronombre aunque nombres a la persona: le di el libro a Juan.
moves.native: Spanish states the pronoun even when the person is named: le di el libro a Juan.

moves.target: Primero el indirecto, después el directo: me lo dio.
moves.native: Indirect first, then direct: me lo dio.

practice.target: Contame qué le regalaste a alguien.
practice.native: Tell me what you gave someone.
Ask me for the salt.
You told him. Say it.

practice.target: Contame algo que le dijiste a alguien.
practice.native: Tell me something you said to someone.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Cuatro pasados y ya está.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Four past tenses and you're set.

moves.target: No es cuánto hace, es cómo lo mirás. Viví diez años allí es pretérito.
moves.native: It's not how long ago — it's how you frame it. Viví diez años allí is preterite.

practice.native: Something you've already done today.
And something you haven't done yet.

practice.target: Contame qué hiciste y qué te falta.
practice.native: Tell me what you've done and what's left.

moves.native: Tell me — the pronoun sticks to the end.
Please. A bare command isn't rude in Spanish, but this softens it.

moves.target: El pronombre se pega atrás: decime, dámelo.
moves.native: The pronoun attaches to the end: decime, dámelo. Note the written accent that appears.

moves.target: Dar una orden directa es normal en español. No suena brusco.
moves.native: A direct command is normal in Spanish. It doesn't land as rude the way it can in English.

practice.native: Ask me to tell you something.
Call me over.
And now politely.
Give me three instructions in a row.

moves.target: Hoy la negativa, que se arma distinto.
moves.native: Today the negative command, which is built completely differently.
Don't speak. The vowels swap: -ar verbs take -es.
Don't worry. The pronoun jumps back in FRONT.
Don't tell me — also used as 'you don't say!'

moves.target: Decime, pero no me digas. El pronombre cambia de lado.
moves.native: Decime, but no me digas. The pronoun switches sides.

moves.target: Las vocales se cruzan. Es lo mismo que vas a usar en el subjuntivo.
moves.native: The vowels swap. It's the same shape you'll use for the subjunctive later.

practice.native: I'm anxious. Calm me down.
Ask me to be quiet.
You don't want to hear the ending.
Reassure me in two sentences.

moves.target: Cerramos con el cuerpo y el dolor.
moves.native: We close with the body and pain.
It hurts me — works exactly like gustar.
The head. Spanish says THE head, not MY head.

moves.target: Me duele la cabeza. El me ya dice que es tuya; mi cabeza sobra.
moves.native: Me duele la cabeza. The me already says it's yours — mi cabeza is redundant.

practice.native: Something hurts. Tell me.
And something plural.

practice.target: Con el artículo, no con mi.
practice.native: With the article, not with mi.
Tell me how you're feeling today.

moves.target: Segunda semana: por y para, las dos que más cuestan.
moves.native: Second week: por and para, the two that cause the most trouble.
Points forward: purpose, destination, deadline, recipient.
Points back or through: cause, exchange, means.
Because of you, on your behalf. Different thing.

moves.target: Antes de un infinitivo de finalidad siempre para: para aprender.
moves.native: Before an infinitive of purpose it's always para: para aprender, never por aprender.

moves.target: Lo hice para ti es un regalo. Lo hice por ti es por vos.
moves.native: Lo hice para ti is a gift. Lo hice por ti is on your behalf.

practice.native: Thank me for something.
What are you studying Spanish for?
You have a present for someone.
Tell me what you're studying Spanish for.

moves.target: Hoy: cómo se dice lo que hace la gente en general.
moves.native: Today: how to say what people do in general.
Is spoken. Where English says 'you' or 'they' vaguely, Spanish uses se.
You can't — the sign on every wall.
How do you say? The most useful question in the language.

moves.target: El verbo concuerda con la cosa: se venden pisos, no se vende pisos.
moves.native: The verb agrees with the thing: se venden pisos, not se vende pisos.

moves.target: Con se no acusás a nadie. Por eso está en todos los carteles.
moves.native: With se you accuse nobody. That's why it's on every sign.

practice.target: Preguntame una palabra que no sabés.
practice.native: Ask me a word you don't know.

practice.target: Una prohibición del lugar donde vivís.
practice.native: A rule where you live.

practice.target: ¿Qué idioma se habla en tu país?
practice.native: What language is spoken in your country?
Ask me three words.

moves.target: Última de la unidad. Instrucciones, salud y reglas.
moves.native: Last of the unit. Instructions, health and rules.
I forgot — literally, it forgot itself on me. Spanish reports accidents this way.

moves.target: Se me cayó, se me olvidó. No es excusa: es como se cuenta un accidente.
moves.native: Se me cayó, se me olvidó. It isn't dodging blame — it's the normal way to report an accident.

practice.native: You forgot your keys.
And on top of that something hurts.

practice.target: Contame un día en que todo salió mal.
practice.native: Tell me about a day when everything went wrong.

moves.target: Unidad diez, la última de este tramo. El futuro de verdad.
moves.native: Unit ten, the last of this stretch. The real future tense.
I will speak. The ending goes on the WHOLE infinitive.
I will eat. One set of endings for all three families.

moves.target: En la calle se usa más voy a. Este tiempo es de escribir y de prometer.
moves.native: In the street, voy a is more common. This tense is for writing and for promises.

moves.target: Las terminaciones van sobre el infinitivo entero: comeré, no comré.
moves.native: The endings go on the whole infinitive: comeré, not comré.

practice.native: Promise me you'll speak to her.

practice.target: ¿Qué vas a hacer el año que viene?
practice.native: What will you do next year?
Where will you live in ten years?

practice.target: Contame tus planes a largo plazo.
practice.native: Tell me your long-term plans.

moves.target: Hoy los irregulares, que son doce y sirven dos veces.
moves.native: Today the irregulars — twelve of them, and they'll serve you twice.
There will be — singular and plural alike, like hay.

moves.target: Estas mismas raíces sirven para el condicional. Se aprenden una vez.
moves.native: These same stems serve the conditional too. You learn them once, they pay twice.

moves.target: Habrá mucha gente. Nunca habrán, igual que hay.
moves.native: Habrá mucha gente — never habrán, just like hay.

practice.native: Will you have time tomorrow?
What will you do on Sunday?
Will there be a lot of people?
Tell me what you'll do this week.

moves.target: Cerramos con el uso que nadie enseña: adivinar.
moves.native: We close with the use nobody teaches: guessing.
He's probably at home. This is the future used as a guess about NOW.
What time do you reckon it is?

moves.target: El futuro también sirve para suponer sobre el presente. Es muy común hablando.
moves.native: The future also expresses a guess about the present. Very common in speech.

practice.native: He's not answering. Make a guess.
You've no watch. Ask.
Guess where I am right now.

moves.target: Segunda semana: el condicional, que es la forma educada.
moves.native: Second week: the conditional, which is how you're polite.
Could I? Much politer than puedo.
If I were you — followed by the conditional.

moves.target: Cuidado: el would de una costumbre pasada en inglés acá es el imperfecto.
moves.native: Careful: English 'would' for a past habit is the imperfect in Spanish, not this tense.

moves.target: Mismas raíces que el futuro, terminaciones del imperfecto.
moves.native: Same stems as the future, endings of the imperfect.

practice.native: Ask me something very politely.
Tell me something you'd like.
Give me advice.

practice.target: Pedime algo como si no me conocieras.
practice.native: Ask me for something as if we'd never met.

moves.target: Hoy: que, la palabra que no se puede saltear.
moves.native: Today: que, the word you can never drop.
That, which, who — for people and things alike.
The book I bought. English drops the that; Spanish cannot.
What — standing for a whole idea.

moves.target: El libro compré no es una frase. Falta el que.
moves.native: El libro compré is not a sentence. The que is missing.

moves.target: En inglés se puede omitir. En español nunca.
moves.native: English can leave it out. Spanish never can.

practice.native: Tell me about something you bought.
The place where you were born.
Something you don't understand.
Describe a person to me using que.

moves.target: Última clase del tramo. Todo lo que sabés, junto.
moves.native: Last class of the stretch. Everything you know, together.
I hope. From here on this opens a whole new mood — the subjunctive.

moves.target: Presente, dos pasados, futuro y condicional. Ya podés contar tu vida entera.
moves.native: Present, two pasts, future and conditional. You can now narrate your whole life.

practice.native: Tell me something you hope for.
And something you'd like.
And one concrete plan.

practice.target: Contame de dónde venís y adónde vas.
practice.native: Tell me where you've come from and where you're going.
